text:
jules: Heads-up - I hit two annoying things while setting up redwoodctl in a Windows service container: 1) the installer created a profile that overwrote my REDWOOD_PROFILE at runtime, and 2) the login flow tried to open a browser which obviously failed inside the service.

omar: can you paste the exact commands you ran? Windows services / containers are tricky with interactive flows.

jules: repro: install MSI in container, set REDWOOD_PROFILE=ci-service, then `redwoodctl config init --from-env`. After that any CLI call logs `Using profile: default` and subsequent calls error with "profile not found: ci-service".

ivy: sounds like the init flow falls back to create a default profile when it can't resolve the env var early in startup. We had similar reports where create+merge logic writes both the env-named profile and a new default.

omar: I remember a race: env var read happens after migration step which rewrites config. If migration adds default and reindexes profiles, the active pointer ends up pointing to default.

jules: yeah. Separately, login behaviour: `redwoodctl login --headless` inside the service logs an attempt to spawn `start`/`explorer` and then sits waiting for callback for 60s before timing out. CI logs show nothing useful.

ivy: for headless we should default to device code if no interactive TTY or if stdout isn't a terminal. For services we must never attempt browser open. Also we should surface the URL + code in the logs in plain text.

omar: agreed. For the profile overwrite bug, quick mitigation: if REDWOOD_PROFILE is set and points to a profile that exists pre-install, don't touch its pointer. If it doesn't exist, create it but do not create a second default. Instead write a warning and exit with code 65 (CONFIG_ERROR).

jules: that would unblock us. Also: could we add a `--no-browser` flag that forces device-code and never attempts to open anything? That would be useful for automation.

ivy: good idea. We'll add `--no-browser` and auto-fallback logic: if not interactive or if `NO_BROWSER=1` -> device flow.

omar: one more small DX nit: when device flow prints the URL we currently wrap at 80 cols with ANSI colors, which breaks some log parsers in our orchestration. Could we add `--plain` output or a machine-readable JSON mode for CI?

jules: JSON would be great: return {"flow":"device","url":"...","user_code":"..."} so orchestrators can post it to an internal auth service.

ops: I'll add integration tests in the container matrix to run `redwoodctl login --headless --no-browser --output json` and assert we get valid JSON quickly. Also will test install+migrate with REDWOOD_PROFILE present.

ivy: plan summary: 1) preserve env-designated profile across migrations or fail fast with config error instead of creating default; 2) add --no-browser and auto-fallback to device-code when non-interactive; 3) add machine-readable output for auth flows (json/plain); 4) improve logs so service/container installs don't hang waiting for GUI.

release-bot: Created issues: #4710 (config: preserve REDWOOD_PROFILE during migrate), #4711 (auth: --no-browser + device-code auto-fallback), #4712 (auth: add --output json for auth flows), #4713 (ci: container integration tests for login + install).

jules: thanks — will validate once patches land. Posting a short service container repro in #4710. :sparkles:
